arguments: {"summary": "Reviewed the spark-core 2.7.1 snapshot (pom.xml line 12; 105 model-visible files under src/main, no tests). One candidate submitted: a provable exception-class mismatch in the copied Jetty URL-decoding helpers used for route parameters, which makes the intended ISO-8859-1 fallback dead code and turns malformed percent-encoded path segments into uncaught exceptions during request construction. Impact is bounded (attacker-triggered 500s / broken decoding, possible secondary NPE in the generic error path), so it is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability. The classic static-file directory-traversal area was traced in depth without finding a working bypass and is listed as an unconfirmed rejected lead.", "candidates": [{"id": "spark-urldecoding-notutf8-class-mismatch", "title": "URI-decode rejection throws Jetty's NotUtf8Exception while UrlDecode catches only the local class, so malformed route parameters raise uncaught exceptions and the ISO-8859-1 fallback is dead", "weakness_type": "Improper exception handling / uncaught exception during input decoding (CWE-248; input-validation class)", "root_cause": "spark.utils.urldecoding.Utf8Appendable is expected (by UrlDecode's catch clause) to signal failures with its own nested spark.utils.urldecoding.Utf8Appendable.NotUtf8Exception, but all three throw sites use the unrelated fully-qualified org.eclipse.jetty.util.Utf8Appendable.NotUtf8Exception (lines 91, 148, 177). UrlDecode.path catches only spark.utils.urldecoding.Utf8Appendable.NotUtf8Exception (UrlDecode.java line 91), which is now never thrown, so the documented decodeISO88591Path fallback is unreachable for rejected/incomplete byte sequences and the thrown IllegalArgumentException escapes the decoder.", "locations": [{"path": "src/main/java/spark/utils/urldecoding/Utf8Appendable.java", "start_line": 86, "end_line": 93}, {"path": "src/main/java/spark/utils/urldecoding/Utf8Appendable.java", "start_line": 143, "end_line": 148}, {"path": "src/main/java/spark/utils/urldecoding/Utf8Appendable.java", "start_line": 161, "end_line": 178}, {"path": "src/main/java/spark/utils/urldecoding/UrlDecode.java", "start_line": 84, "end_line": 94}, {"path": "src/main/java/spark/Request.java", "start_line": 119, "end_line": 125}, {"path": "src/main/java/spark/Request.java", "start_line": 495, "end_line": 514}, {"path": "src/main/java/spark/http/matching/Routes.java", "start_line": 49, "end_line": 57}, {"path": "src/main/java/spark/http/matching/MatcherFilter.java", "start_line": 126, "end_line": 147}, {"path": "src/main/java/spark/http/matching/GeneralError.java", "start_line": 37, "end_line": 66}], "attacker_control": "The remote client controls the raw request URI. For any route containing a parameter or splat (e.g. get(\"/hello/:name\")), the raw matched path segment is passed to UrlDecode.path from Request.getParams (Request.java 498-511). A segment containing invalid UTF-8 percent escapes, such as %FF (UTF8_REJECT in appendByte) or %C3%28 (ASCII byte while a multibyte sequence is pending, drive TRANS_TABLE to REJECT), reaches the throw sites; %C3 at the end reaches checkState(). All of these throw Jetty's NotUtf8Exception, which UrlDecode does not catch.", "prerequisites": "An application route with :param or * matching the crafted path (or a matching before filter, which also builds a Request the same way); the malformed bytes must be present in the raw getRequestURI value used for route matching. The secondary NPE in the error path additionally requires an application-registered IllegalArgumentException handler; the plain 500 needs no extra configuration.", "trace": "Request constructor -> changeMatch (Request.java 119-125) -> getParams (495-514) -> UrlDecode.path(request.get(i)) -> Utf8StringBuilder/Utf8Appendable.appendByte or checkState -> throws org.eclipse.jetty.util.Utf8Appendable.NotUtf8Exception -> UrlDecode.java:91 catch (spark.utils.urldecoding.Utf8Appendable.NotUtf8Exception) does not match -> propagates through RequestResponseFactory.create into Routes.execute (Routes.java 52-53) or BeforeFilters.execute (BeforeFilters.java 41) -> MatcherFilter generic catch (Exception) at 137-145 -> GeneralError.modify sets 500 or runs the user handler. In GeneralError the per-request ResponseWrapper delegate is still null on this path, so user-handler/response access can raise a secondary NPE.", "impact": "Availability/robustness for attacker-selected requests: a route-parameter request carrying malformed UTF-8 percent-encoding produces an unhandled IllegalArgumentException (HTTP 500) instead of the intended permissive ISO-8859-1-decoded parameter, and the decodeISO88591Path fallback never executes. If an application registered an exception handler for IllegalArgumentException, that handler runs against Request/Response wrappers whose delegates were not installed yet, which can produce a secondary NPE and defeat the handler's intended response. No data disclosure or privilege escalation demonstrated.", "counterevidence_checked": "Confirmed via text search that only Utf8Appendable.java references the Jetty FQN and that the local nested NotUtf8Exception class is otherwise unused (dead), while UrlDecode.java:91 catches the local class. Confirmed reachability only when a parameterised route/wildcard matches the malformed URI, and that MatcherFilter catches the exception generically (500, not process crash). Checked that UrlDecode also throws its own uncaught IllegalArgumentException(\"Bad URI % encoding\") for a dangling %, i.e. the decoder is generally not exception-tolerant; the class mismatch specifically defeats the UTF-8 rejection fallback. Checked the rest of the request path (UriPath.canonical, cleanPath, MimeParse, MimeType regex, QueryParamsMap, IOUtils, serializers) for comparable defects.", "confidence": "medium", "unverified": "Not runtime-confirmed: no server was executed and no payloads were sent, so the 500/dead-fallback behaviour and the secondary NPE are argued from source only. Whether Jetty 9.4.6 delivers the malformed raw segment to route matching is inferred, not tested. I could not determine whether this FQN usage is original upstream 2.7.1 code or a modification, so the practical severity (bounded per-request failure vs. a deeper decoding bypass) remains uncertain."}], "rejected_leads": [{"lead": "Static-file path traversal in spark/resource/ClassPathResourceHandler.java, spark/resource/ExternalResourceHandler.java, spark/staticfiles/DirectoryTraversal.java, UriPath.canonical and StringUtils.cleanPath (the 2.7.x traversal area, incl. the CVE-2018-9159 window).", "reason": "I traced the full request path (AbstractResourceHandler.getResource -> servletPath+pathInfo -> UriPath.canonical -> addPaths -> ClassPathResource/ExternalResource cleanPath -> DirectoryTraversal prefix check) and could not construct a working escape: canonical() removes \".\"/\"..\" segments and returns null above the root, cleanPath resolves remaining \"..\" against the drive/root prefix (its colon-prefix branch only preserves \"..\" where the resulting name contains an invalid path character and is not openable), and both traversal checks reject the resulting escaped strings. Residual hardening concerns not turned into an exploit: the plain String.startsWith prefix comparison has no separator boundary (folder \"www\" would match \"www-private\"), Paths.get(path).toAbsolutePath() is compared lexically without normalize()/toRealPath() so symlinks inside the served folder are followed, and StaticFilesFolder.local/external are shared mutable statics across Service instances (a second Service can perturb another's checks). No candidate submitted for this because no attacker-reachable escape was demonstrated."}, {"lead": "Unconditional trust of client-supplied forwarding headers via new ForwardedRequestCustomizer() in spark/embeddedserver/jetty/SocketConnectorFactory.java (createHttpConnectionFactory, lines 106-110) combined with Request.ip()/scheme()/port()/raw().", "reason": "A remote client can send X-Forwarded-For/X-Forwarded-Proto/X-Forwarded-Host and Jetty will override getRemoteAddr()/scheme/server name/port when Spark is exposed directly, so applications using request.ip() for ACLs, rate limiting or audit logging trust attacker-controlled values. Classified as an unconfirmed trust-boundary/configuration concern rather than the selected candidate: it is deliberate upstream behaviour for reverse-proxy deployments, exploitation requires the application to rely on those values, and no affected application code exists in this snapshot."}, {"lead": "GzipUtils.checkAndWrap substring matching for Accept-Encoding (spark/utils/GzipUtils.java lines 59-83, StringMatch uses s.contains(\"gzip\")) and unconditional gzip for static files (requireWantsHeader=false from StaticFilesConfiguration.java line 101).", "reason": "Accept-Encoding: gzip;q=0 or unrelated tokens containing \"gzip\" still trigger compression, a protocol violation that can break clients or waste CPU, but no confidentiality/integrity/availability impact was established and the code path performs no attacker-controlled writes."}, {"lead": "Memory/recursion exhaustion candidates: HttpRequestWrapper caching the whole non-chunked, non-multipart request body (spark/embeddedserver/jetty/HttpRequestWrapper.java lines 49-74) and recursive QueryParamsMap.loadKeys for deeply nested keys (spark/QueryParamsMap.java lines 109-124).", "reason": "Both are attacker-influenced resource-consumption patterns bounded by the container's request-size/URI limits; I could not show a concrete OOM/StackOverflow threshold or a security-relevant consequence beyond degrading the single request, so they remain unconfirmed."}, {"lead": "Case-insensitive X-HTTP-Method-Override handling in MatcherFilter (lines 48-49, 195-202) and Response.redirect(String, int) setting Location before sendError (spark/Response.java 134-146).", "reason": "Both are API-level behaviours with no framework-level validation defect: method override requires a custom header an attacker cannot add cross-site, and redirect targets are developer supplied; no evidence of attacker-controlled header/CRLF injection (Jetty rejects invalid header values)."}], "coverage_summary": "All 105 model-visible files under src/main/java were enumerated; I read or searched every area relevant to untrusted input: request lifecycle (MatcherFilter, Body, Halt, GeneralError, Before/After/AfterAfter filters, RouteContext, wrappers), routing (Routable, Service, Routes, RouteEntry, RouteMatch, HttpMethod, SparkUtils, FilterTools, SparkFilter), resource/static-file handling (StaticFilesConfiguration, DirectoryTraversal, StaticFilesFolder, ClassPathResourceHandler, ExternalResourceHandler, ClassPathResource, ExternalResource, AbstractFileResolvingResource, AbstractResourceHandler.addPaths, UriPath, StringUtils.cleanPath), parameter/URI decoding (Request, QueryParamsMap, UrlDecode, Utf8Appendable, Utf8StringBuilder, TypeUtil), serialization, MIME handling (MimeType, MimeParse), GzipUtils, Session, Response/Redirect, embedded Jetty wiring (SocketConnectorFactory, EmbeddedJettyServer, JettyHandler, HttpRequestWrapper, websocket factories), and utility copies (IOUtils, ResourceUtils, ClassUtils, CollectionUtils, ObjectUtils, Assert). Build files (pom.xml, .travis.yml) and README were read for version/config context. Build/test execution, dependency source (Jetty/Spring), and servlet-container behaviour were out of scope.", "limitations": ["No code was executed, built, or fuzzed; all conclusions (including the submitted candidate's HTTP-500/secondary-NPE behaviour) are static-source arguments and would need runtime confirmation.", "No tests are present in the snapshot (src/main only), so intended behaviour and regression expectations could not be cross-checked.", "Third-party dependency behaviour (Jetty 9.4.6.v20170531 URI parsing/decoding, ServletContextHandler, WebSocket) was reasoned from call sites only; the exact form of pathInfo/getRequestURI values for malformed encodings was not verified.", "Whether the Utf8Appendable FQN throw sites are original upstream code or a modification could not be determined without external history, which affects severity classification.", "The static-file traversal area was reviewed defensively but a determined black-box tester might reach the prefix-check/symlink/shared-static-state concerns in ways not demonstrable from source alone.", "No inspection of sibling configurations, patches, CVE records, or prior runs was performed, per the review conditions."]}
